blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the 9th term of the harmonic sequence: \(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{7}, \dots\)
blocks.explanation:
A harmonic sequence (H.P.) is a list whose reciprocals form an A.P.
We must find the 9th term.
Plan: take reciprocals, find the 9th term of that A.P., then take the reciprocal again.
steps:
Given: the H.P. \(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{7}, \dots\)
To find: its 9th term.
Method: There is no direct formula for the terms of an H.P.; we use the A.P. of reciprocals and \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\).

Write the reciprocals
\[3, \; 5, \; 7, \; \dots\]
Why: The reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{3}\) is 3, of \(\frac{1}{5}\) is 5, and so on. By definition these form an A.P.

Find \(a_1\) and \(d\) of the A.P.
\[a_1 = 3\]
\[d = 5 - 3 = 2\]
Why: \(d\) is any term minus the term before it; \(7 - 5 = 2\) too.

Find the 9th term of the A.P.
\[a_9 = a_1 + 8d\]
\[= 3 + 8(2) = 19\]
Why: From the 1st to the 9th term there are 8 steps of \(d\).

Take the reciprocal
\[\text{9th term of H.P.} = \dfrac{1}{19}\]
Why: The H.P. term is the reciprocal of the matching A.P. term.
Check: the A.P. 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19 has 19 as its 9th entry, so the H.P. has \(\frac{1}{19}\) in 9th place. It agrees with the answer key.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the 9th term of the harmonic sequence: \(-\frac{1}{5}, -\frac{1}{3}, -1, \dots\)
blocks.explanation:
Again an H.P., now with negative terms.
We must find the 9th term.
Plan: reciprocals form an A.P.; find its 9th term and invert it.
steps:
Given: the H.P. \(-\frac{1}{5}, -\frac{1}{3}, -1, \dots\)
To find: its 9th term.
Method: Reciprocals form an A.P.; use \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) and invert.

Write the reciprocals
\[-5, \; -3, \; -1, \; \dots\]
Why: The reciprocal of \(-\frac{1}{5}\) is \(-5\); the sign stays with the number. \(-1\) is its own reciprocal.

Find \(a_1\) and \(d\)
\[a_1 = -5\]
\[d = -3 - (-5) = 2\]
Why: Second minus first; \(-1 - (-3) = 2\) as well, so it is an A.P.

Find the 9th term of the A.P.
\[a_9 = -5 + 8(2)\]
\[= -5 + 16 = 11\]
Why: 8 steps of 2 from the first term.

Take the reciprocal
\[\text{9th term of H.P.} = \dfrac{1}{11}\]
Why: Invert the A.P. term to return to the H.P.
Check: the A.P. continues \(-5, -3, -1, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11\); the 9th entry is 11, so the H.P. term is \(\frac{1}{11}\). It agrees with the answer key.
